title: APN permutations in even dimensions greater than six
summary: Determine whether an almost perfect nonlinear permutation exists in any even dimension greater than six.

formal_statement.body: Does there exist an integer $m>3$ and a permutation $F:\mathbb F_2^{2m}\to\mathbb F_2^{2m}$ that is almost perfect nonlinear? Construct one such permutation, or prove that no APN permutation exists in any even dimension $2m>6$.

scope.domain: Almost perfect nonlinear permutations in even dimensions
assumptions: m is an integer greater than 3
F is a permutation of F_2^{2m}
scope.unresolved_remainder: The scalar trace-product switching family of the Gold cube yields no APN map for even dimensions at least ten, and its marked dimension-eight maps are nonpermutations. APN-permutation existence outside this strict construction mechanism remains open in every even dimension greater than six.

provenance.note: The 2022 and 2026 TIT papers restate the Big APN problem and point to earlier open-problem literature; Carlet's 2015 chapter is the earliest text-confirmed statement in this provenance trace.
